rationale: Each damage event matching Polyraptor's trigger condition automatically triggers a new copy-creating ability (603.2), and the chain stops when Forerunner of the Empire has lethal damage marked on it and is destroyed as a state-based action (704.5g).

Desert of the Mindful's non-mana activated ability makes it a land with an activated ability that isn't a mana ability under the 605.1a definition, and 502.3 states effects can keep permanents from untapping during the untap step.

The claim is that a cost reduction never changes the spell's mana cost: 202.1a defines the mana cost as the symbols on the object, 118.7 says paying a changed or reduced cost still counts as paying the original, and 601.2f keeps the total cost separate from the mana cost.
107.4f states Phyrexian mana symbols are colored mana symbols ({B/P} is black), so Surgical Extraction's mana cost contains one black symbol for Drought to count.
With empty libraries the reveal instruction can't be performed and is ignored (101.3), so no player revealed a card and no player meets the highest-mana-value condition to change targets.

Soul-Scar Mage's ability is a replacement effect; 614.1 says such effects replace the event with a different one and 614.6 states a replaced event never happens, so the Squire was never dealt damage and Annihilating Fire's dealt-damage-this-way exile clause doesn't apply.
701.43a defines exerting as choosing that the permanent won't untap during your next untap step, which is the exerting player's untap step only.

601.2f states the total cost is the mana cost plus all additional costs, and 601.2h states the player pays those costs in any order, so all the creature cards are exiled as a single payment and Desecrated Tomb triggers once.

514.2 ends the until-end-of-turn crew effect during cleanup, while the Aura's copy effect is a static-ability continuous effect that keeps applying (604.1) in layer 1a (613.2a), leaving the permanent a Barktooth Warbeard.

601.2h has costs (the discard) paid during casting, while 601.2i states the spell only becomes cast once steps 601.2a-h are complete, so Soul Sculptor's effect was still on Confessor when the discard happened.

601.2i fixes the moment the spell becomes cast, which is when Soul Sculptor's effect ends, and 603.10/603.2 state trigger conditions are checked against objects as they exist immediately after that event, when Mona Lisa has its abilities back.

401.2 states players can't change the order of cards in a library, so looking at the top five doesn't reorder them; Lantern of Insight's static ability applies continuously (604.1), so the next card down becomes revealed once the first one leaves.

700.2d states a mode chosen multiple times is treated as appearing that many times in sequence, and 701.6a states countering removes the spell from the stack to the graveyard, so the later instances find no spell to counter and Baral triggers once.
702.123a gives fabricate's exact wording (you may put N +1/+1 counters on it; if you don't, create N Servo tokens), which is what the answer rests on when counters can't be placed.

Two replacement effects, The Flame of Keld and Soul-Scar Mage, want to modify the same damage event, so 616.1 gives the affected object's controller the choice of which to apply first and re-checks which remain applicable.

616.1 lets the controller order the two enters-the-battlefield replacement effects, and 614.12 states the game determines applicable effects by checking the permanent as it would exist taking already-applied replacement effects into account, so devour's sacrifice isn't performed yet and Metallic Mimic still applies.
305.6 states a land with a basic land type has the intrinsic tap-for-mana ability, and 613.1f puts ability-removing effects in layer 6, so Overwhelming Splendor strips that intrinsic ability.

702.119a defines emerge's cost reduction by the sacrificed creature's mana value; 601.2b and 702.119c state the creature to sacrifice is chosen when the emerge cost is chosen, before costs are paid, so a creature not yet on the battlefield can't be picked.
903.10a states a player dealt 21 or more combat damage by the same commander loses the game, with no reference to who controls or owns that commander.

Infect converts the damage into a poison counter (702.90b), ten or more poison counters is a state-based loss (704.5c) that Angel's Grace holds off, and 514.2 ends the this-turn effect in cleanup so the state-based action check in 514.3a then kills Nico.

702.82a states devour's sacrifice happens as the permanent enters, so the Hatchling is on the battlefield simultaneously; 603.8 states a state trigger only triggers while the game state matches its condition, and it never does.

The Licid stops being a creature, so the attachment fails (303.4j an effect can't attach an Aura to something it can't legally enchant; 303.4d an Aura can't enchant itself), and 704.5m puts an unattached Aura into its owner's graveyard as a state-based action.

702.16a states protection from a card type applies to sources not on the battlefield that are of that type, covering Ulamog as a creature spell, and 702.16b states such a permanent can't be targeted by abilities from a source with that quality.
113.2c states that if an object has multiple instances of the same ability, each instance functions independently, so two Soul Links give two separate triggers.
701.27f states an activated ability of a permanent transforms it only if it hasn't already transformed since that ability was put onto the stack, so the second activation does nothing.
Ichorid's ability has an intervening if clause; 603.4 states the condition is rechecked as the ability resolves and the ability is removed from the stack and does nothing if it's false.

113.6 states abilities of objects other than instants and sorceries usually function only while on the battlefield, so Death's Shadow's static power/toughness ability doesn't apply while the card is in exile.

The permission comes from the resolved trigger's continuous effect, which lasts for its stated duration (611.2a); 113.7a states the ability exists independently of its source, so removing the Flamespeaker doesn't affect it.
Carpet of Flowers' intervening if clause is checked when the trigger event occurs (603.4); having added no mana means the condition is still true when the second main phase begins.
106.12b states a tapped-for-mana replacement effect only modifies the mana production event while such an ability is resolving and producing mana, and Gaea's Cradle with no creatures produces none.
106.12a states an ability that triggers when a permanent is tapped for mana triggers only when such a mana ability resolves and produces mana, which Gaea's Cradle with no creatures doesn't.

400.7 states an object changing zones becomes a new object, ending the Mirrorweave copy effect, and 702.52a states dredge functions only while the card with dredge is in a graveyard, which the token never is.

603.10 and 603.10a state leaves-the-battlefield triggers look back in time to the game state immediately before the event, when Bridge from Below was still on the battlefield rather than in the graveyard.
Both 702.4b and 510.4 state that double strike causes the combat phase to get a second combat damage step, giving Avery a window between the two damage steps.

702.34a states flashback's second ability exiles the card as it leaves the stack only if that spell's flashback cost was paid, and 400.7 states the card Spell Queller exiled is a new object, so that replacement no longer applies and the recast spell goes to the graveyard.

702.95a gives soulbond's wording: the ability only triggers when the creature enters and only if another unpaired creature is already controlled, so a permanent that becomes a creature later can't be paired.
702.95a's second soulbond ability pairs only the creature that caused it to trigger, and 702.95e states a paired creature becomes unpaired when the creature it's paired with leaves the battlefield.

702.62a states the suspend trigger lets you play the card as that trigger resolves, and 608.1 states only the top object of the stack resolves at a time, so the second trigger waits until the first Rift Bolt has left the stack.
Mana Reflection and Damping Sphere are two replacement effects modifying the same mana-production event, so 616.1 gives the affected player the choice of which to apply first.
Vengevine's intervening if clause is checked when the trigger event occurs (603.4); the fourth creature spell of the turn isn't the second, so the ability never triggers.

116.2f and 702.62a state that exiling a card with suspend is a special action that doesn't use the stack, and 116.1 states special actions are taken while a player has priority and don't use the stack, so there is no window to respond.

707.12 states a copy a player is instructed to cast is created in the same zone the object is in, here exile, and 707.10a states a copy of a card in any zone other than the stack or battlefield ceases to exist as a state-based action.

702.35a gives madness's wording: the discard is replaced with exiling the card, then its owner may cast it for the madness cost or it is put into the graveyard, which is exactly the sequence in the answer.

603.2 states an ability triggers whenever a game event matches its trigger event; one attack declaration is one event, so Frenzied Goblin's ability triggers once and the optional payment is made on that single resolution.
603.7a states a delayed triggered ability is only created when the spell or ability creating it resolves and won't trigger for an event that happened beforehand, so the untap set up no destruction.
603.3b states a player puts the triggered abilities they control on the stack in any order they choose, so Augustine picks which return-to-battlefield trigger resolves first.

109.5 states you and your on an object refer to the object's controller, so the Aura's upkeep trigger is Natasha's; 113.7a and 608.2h state that when the source is no longer in the zone it was expected to be in, its last known information, including infect, is used.
400.7 states the exiled and returned creature is a new object, and 608.2b states a spell whose targets are all illegal on resolution doesn't resolve and is put into its owner's graveyard.

603.3b states the controller of multiple triggered abilities puts them on the stack in any order they choose, so Annie picks which return trigger resolves and the other finds nothing in the graveyard.

603.2 with 603.10 state trigger conditions are matched against the objects as they exist immediately after the event, so the ability gained by being turned face up is present when that event is checked.
